question: In the DX-Scorecard MBR "Pull data & start" collection screen (per-bucket Queued to Collecting to "N values pulled" behind a progress bar), does collection invoke the real per-KPI CLI endpoint POST /__collect/<kpiId> (up to ~240s each), the stub POST /__mbr/refresh pipeline, or both, and how is the mockup's "~30s" hint and per-bucket progress reconciled with real per-KPI collection latency?
recommendation: Drive the MBR 'Pull data & start' screen off the REAL per-KPI endpoint POST /__collect/<kpiId> (the shelled-out Copilot CLI, one KPI at a time), NOT the stub POST /__mbr/refresh, and model per-bucket progress as an aggregation over those sequential per-KPI runs. Because a real collect is minutes, not seconds, drop the mockup's misleading '~30s' hint: show per-KPI Queued→Collecting→done substeps (each bounded by the 240s CLI timeout), let the bar advance as each KPI completes, and surface an honest estimate (~2–4 min per KPI, roughly M×2.5min total) rather than a single 30s promise.
supporting_points: Two distinct, real pipelines exist and today they are NOT interchangeable: collectKpi() in src/lib/devWrite.ts POSTs to the per-KPI '/__collect/<kpiId>' endpoint (dev-write-plugin dispatchCollect shells out to Copilot CLI, DEFAULT_COLLECT_TIMEOUT_MS = 240_000ms, ~2.5min measured per KPI, concurrency 1) and is wired into UpdateKpisView's 'Update all automatically' sweep; MbrBuilderView instead calls refreshMbr() → POST '/__mbr/refresh', a fast stub that only emits readings for a tiny WIRED_METRIC_IDS set while every other KPI carries forward — so for real per-value collection the MBR screen must use /__collect, treating /__mbr/refresh (or its stub source) only as a carry-forward/seed path, not the collection engine.

The '~30s' hint and quick spinner come from the mockup, where collection is faked (docs/mocks/update-kpis.html: 'collection is simulated (no real Copilot CLI shells out)'; update-kpis.js resolves each collect in 700–1600ms and even the timeout case cites 20s). This is fiction: DEFAULT_COLLECT_TIMEOUT_MS = 240s and the code comment documents ~2.5min of real Kusto queries per KPI, so a '~30s' promise cannot be honored by the real endpoint and should be replaced with a realistic per-KPI estimate.

Per-bucket 'Queued → Collecting → N values pulled' should be composed from sequential per-KPI /__collect calls (each returning a validated {value, asOf} or a per-KPI 502/timeout failure), advancing the progress bar as individual KPIs finish rather than treating a bucket as one atomic ~30s step — mirroring UpdateKpisView's existing concurrency-1 sweep and per-row Collecting→success/failed states, which already reconcile UI progress with the true 240s-bounded per-KPI latency.
